tables.description: Basic shape: saw. The ramp -1..1, harmonics falling as 1/k.

tables.name: Square
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: Basic shape: square. Odd harmonics only, falling as 1/k.

tables.name: Triangle
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: Basic shape: triangle. Odd harmonics falling as 1/k^2.

tables.name: Rectified
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: Full-wave rectified sine: an octave-up companion to Sine. Shipped as 16-bit PCM, the format's other supported encoding, so the reader's 16-bit path is exercised by our own content and not only by the factory corpus.

tables.name: FM Morph
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: Phase-modulated sine; the modulation index rises from 0 to 8 across the frames.

tables.name: Sync Sweep
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: A sine read through a rising sync ratio, 1x to 8x across the frames.

tables.name: PWM Morph
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: Pulse width sweeping 5% to 95% across the frames.

tables.name: Fold Drive
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: Symmetric tanh folder; drive rises from 1x to 13x across the frames.

tables.name: Harmonic Sweep
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: Additive: a pure sine whose second, third, fifth and eighth harmonics fade in across the frames, so the position is a brightness control.

tables.name: Formant Sweep
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: A single resonant peak walked up the harmonic series from the first to the fourteenth, which is what a vowel sweep is when it is done additively.

tables.name: Formant High
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: The same additive peak, but starting at the fifth harmonic and moving to the eleventh: the bright half of the vowel sweep, on its own.

tables.name: Vocal Stack
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: Two fixed formants: one held at the second harmonic, one walked from the sixth to the twelfth. Choirs, not vowels.

tables.name: Odd Stack
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: Odd harmonics only, appearing with the frame: the hollow, clarinet-like end of the additive family.

tables.name: Saw Fade
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: An eight-harmonic saw fading into its own fundamental: the plainest morph in the library, and the one a bass or a lead wants.

tables.name: Square Fade
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: Square crossfaded into sine across the frames. Signed, so its middle frame is quieter than either end — a morph that thins as it opens.

tables.name: Bit Crush
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: A ramp quantised onto fewer and fewer levels as the frame rises: 32 steps down to 2, which is arithmetic rather than a bit-crusher effect.

tables.name: Bend Sweep
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: A sine whose phase is warped about the centre, so the zero crossings crowd together as the frame opens while the cycle stays seamless at the edges.

tables.name: Ring Swell
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: A sine ring-modulated by a quotient of itself and a rising multiplier: the fundamental stays, and a clash of inharmonic partials grows around it.

tables.name: Glass Stack
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: The fundamental with 5th, 11th, 13th and 17th harmonics stacked on top: high, thin and glassy at the top of its sweep.

tables.name: Noise Blend
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: A sine dissolving into deterministic noise — a hash of the sample index, not a random number, so the table regenerates byte for byte.

tables.name: Dust
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: The same hash with nothing under it: eight frames of flat noise, for the presets that want a texture rather than a tone.

tables.name: Growl Fold
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: A ramp through a tanh saturator, driven from 1x to 11x: the saw-side companion to Fold Drive, which does the same to a sine.

tables.name: Pulse Grit
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: A pulse narrowing from 50% to 5% across the frames — the other half of the pulse-width family from PWM Morph, which runs 5% to 95%.

tables.name: Sync Saw
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: A saw read through a rising sync ratio, 1x to 14x. Sync Sweep does the same to a sine, and the two are different sounds.

tables.name: Metal Sync
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: The same sync read at **half-integer** ratios from 2.5 to 11.5, which puts the cycle's partials between the harmonics instead of on them.

tables.name: Sparkle
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: A sine replaced by the 19th and 23rd harmonics as the frame rises: air, and nothing else, at the top of its sweep.

tables.name: Fallback Shapes
tables.origin: authored for xerum: generated from the formula recorded here by tools/wavetable-author.cpp
tables.description: The fallback: sine, triangle, saw and square, for a reference that cannot be resolved.
